Please review the following manuscript I wrote.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b03/review-experiment-t56i8jpn/call-e321148abc60449c972fa46c37adb50b/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -l manuscript.pdf; command -v pdftotext; command -v pdftoppm; command -v pdfinfo; command -v python3'

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
parts=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
    text=p.extract_text()
    Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i+1:02d}.txt').write_text(text)
    parts.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i+1} =====\\n\\n'+text)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(parts))
print(''.join(parts[:3]))
PY"

strengths: AVIS is a meaningful extension of audio-visual segmentation: distinguishing individual sounding objects and preserving their identities introduces capabilities beyond semantic masks. The task has potential value for video editing and multimodal scene understanding.

AVISeg provides a useful initial annotation effort: 117 annotated videos, 6,973 frames, 281 objects, and 15,355 masks. The broader collection includes five scenarios and averages 62.6 seconds per video, expanding the temporal scope of short-clip audio-visual segmentation.

The Mask2Former baseline with TPAVI fusion and audio-conditioned queries is a reasonable starting point. Table 1 establishes initial reference results of 31.5 AP with ResNet-50 and 35.6 AP with Swin-Base.

The spatiotemporal IoU in Equation (2), including empty-mask padding outside activity intervals, appropriately evaluates complete instance tracks. Reporting AP across IoU thresholds and AR at different detection budgets provides useful complementary measurements.
weaknesses: The central role of audio is unverified. Table 1 compares only two visual backbones; there is no matched vision-only baseline, muted or mismatched audio control, or ablation of TPAVI and audio-conditioned queries. Consequently, the results cannot establish whether the model uses sound to select active instances and suppress silent visible objects. Together with the annotation concerns below, this substantive validation gap determines the weak-reject recommendation despite the worthwhile task contribution.

The benchmark's ground-truth semantics are insufficiently documented. Section 3 identifies a SAM-based annotation tool but does not explain how annotators establish per-instance audibility, handle overlapping sources and intermittent sound, preserve identities across silence or occlusion, or verify annotation quality. Accurate object contours alone do not establish accurate sound-source correspondence. This is particularly consequential because the dataset is the primary original contribution.

The evaluated benchmark is substantially smaller than the collected pool: only 117 of 1,258 videos are annotated, with 84 training and 33 testing videos. Figure 3 does not establish category coverage within these splits, and the manuscript lacks split-selection details and statistics on simultaneous same-class sources. Aggregate AP also leaves performance on long sequences and sound-activity transitions unresolved. These omissions limit interpretation of the claimed breadth and difficulty; small size alone is not the objection.

Reproducibility remains incomplete despite the reported optimizer and training schedule. Equation (1) leaves the contraction and projection dimensions unclear, and the time-indexed learnable queries are not adequately explained when moving from two-frame training to variable-length whole-video inference. Audio-window alignment is also unspecified. No dataset access location, split lists, or implementation release location is supplied, limiting the benchmark's practical reuse.

A smaller presentation issue is the mismatch between Section 5.2 and Figure 6: the text describes raw-frame, ground-truth, and prediction columns, while the displayed columns represent time and the comparison rows are unlabeled. This makes the qualitative evidence difficult to interpret, but is a correctable presentation refinement rather than a principal reason for rejection.
